checkable: Every budget category total is at or below the cap the call sets for it.
Each requirement in the list has a quoted passage from the draft that satisfies it.
The narrative page count is at or below the page limit quoted from the call.
partly: Every requirement is met and the proposal is likely to impress the review panel.
The budget is under every cap and spent wisely.
not: The proposal has a good chance of being funded.
The science is novel and important.
The reviewers will find the writing persuasive.

checkable: No ingredient in any of the seven dinners is a listed allergen.
The shopping list total is at or below the weekly budget in the request.
Every packaged item on the shopping list has been checked for a 'may contain' warning naming a listed allergen, and none has one.
partly: The meals avoid every listed allergen and the family will enjoy them.
The total is within budget and the recipes are not too hard to cook.
not: The meal plan is healthy and balanced.
The children will like the dinners.
The plan is good value.

checkable: Each quote appears in the transcript with exactly the same words and the speaker the transcript gives.
Every segment start timestamp is within 15 seconds of the moment the topic changes in the transcript.
The number of segments is between 5 and 10.
partly: The quotes match the transcript word for word and are the most memorable lines of the episode.
Timestamps are accurate and the segment titles are catchy.
not: The show notes will attract new listeners.
The summaries capture the spirit of the conversation.
The episode is well represented.

checkable: The three shortlisted listings have the three highest scores.
Each shortlisted listing's rent is at or below the budget in the request.
No shortlisted listing has a must-have field marked unknown.
partly: The shortlist holds the top three scores and the renter would be happy living in any of them.
All three are within budget and in nice neighbourhoods.
not: The shortlisted apartments are good choices.
The renter will get one of these apartments.
The scoring reflects what matters most.

checkable: Every test on the flaky list passes in all 30 reruns.
No test outside the flaky list fails in any of the 30 reruns.
Each fix's diff touches only test files or the source file named in its cause.
partly: All flaky tests pass 30 times and the fixes follow best practice.
The reruns are green and the root causes are convincing.
not: The test suite is now reliable.
The fixes are elegant.
The flakiness will not come back.

checkable: Every route in the public route list has a proposed limit.
Each proposed limit is at least twice the p99 requests per minute of its route.
No proposed limit is below the logged peak of any authenticated client on that route.
partly: Every route has a limit and the limits are fair to heavy users.
The limits are above every logged peak and strike the right balance.
not: The limits will stop abuse.
Clients will not be annoyed by the limits.
The configuration is appropriate for the business.

checkable: Every readable receipt appears in exactly one category.
Each category total equals the sum of the amounts of its receipts.
No deductible category total is above the cap given for it in the rules.
partly: The totals add up and the categorisation is defensible to an auditor.
Every receipt is placed once and in the most sensible category.
not: The tax return will be accepted.
The user has claimed everything they are entitled to.
The categorisation is reasonable.
